title: Saturday repair café: the rain plan
premise: A brief Thursday evening planning call between three fictional volunteers. Saturday's monthly repair café was advertised for 10 a.m.–1 p.m. in the community centre courtyard. Rain is now likely, and the only indoor room is occupied until 10:30. The team must settle a workable opening time and handle the few affected bookings.

speakers.label: Maya
speakers.voiceDirection: Adult woman, conversational British English. Warm but practical. Thinking with the others rather than chairing a formal meeting. Ordinary pace; let the small self-correction land naturally.

speakers.label: Jonah
speakers.voiceDirection: Adult man, conversational British English. Calm, slightly lower voice; direct about physical constraints without sounding stern. Unhurried, with natural clause breaks.

speakers.label: Tess
speakers.voiceDirection: Adult woman, conversational British English, clearly distinct from Maya. A little quicker and brighter. Checks the booking list while talking; practical, attentive, never announcer-like.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So, Saturday. I think we have to give up on the courtyard. The forecast's got worse. We can have the small hall, but the craft group are in there until half past ten, and that's when they finish, not when the room's clear.

interjections.speaker: tess
interjections.direction: Quiet acknowledgement, overlapping Maya as she continues with 'and that's'.

turns.speaker: jonah
turns.text: Then eleven's the earliest. We need to get the tables in, run the cables... I'd rather not have people waiting around us while we do that.

turns.speaker: tess
turns.text: Hang on, let me check who's booked before eleven. Three. Two bikes and a toaster. Are we taking bikes inside?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Could they go under the awning?

turns.speaker: jonah
turns.text: With the repair stands there, we'd be blocking the doorway. And rain comes in sideways under that thing. I think we have to cancel the bikes this time.

interjections.speaker: maya
interjections.direction: Soft agreement; Jonah continues without yielding the floor.

turns.speaker: tess
turns.text: Okay. I'll ring those two, then. I don't want them cycling over in the rain for nothing. Next month's session, or do we know somewhere sooner?

turns.speaker: jonah
turns.text: There's the bike workshop at the library next weekend. I'll check they've got spaces before we send anyone there.

turns.speaker: tess
turns.text: Thanks. And I've got eleven fifteen free for the toaster, if that suits them. Everything after eleven can stay as it is.

interjections.speaker: jonah
interjections.direction: Brief listening sound, under Tess's continuing phrase 'for the toaster'.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: How many tables can we actually fit?

turns.speaker: jonah
turns.text: Four comfortably. Two for electrical repairs, one for sewing, one for intake. No spare table for people to leave things on.

turns.speaker: tess
turns.text: That's fine. I'll keep the waiting list at the desk. People need to stay with their stuff anyway.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I'll update the website and the neighbourhood group tonight. And put a sign on the courtyard gate. Actually, I'll be there from ten until we open, because someone will have seen the old time.

interjections.speaker: tess
interjections.direction: Understated acknowledgement as Maya continues 'because someone'.

turns.speaker: jonah
turns.text: I'll tell the repair volunteers half ten for setup. Still finishing at one?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Yes, we can't keep everyone late.

turns.speaker: tess
turns.text: Last walk-ins at quarter past twelve, then? We can have a look, but I won't promise we'll fix it.

turns.speaker: jonah
turns.text: Exactly. And we stop taking things earlier if the queue's full.

turns.speaker: tess
turns.text: Good. I'll make those three calls now.
